newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crude prices rise with NYMEX highs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crude prices rise with NYMEX highs.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices rose with NYMEX futures Monday, after the front-month contract erased Friday's slight loss to hit a contract high of $25.23.
But western markets remained sleepy, with traders still attending industry conferences and little pressure early in the month to buy oil for November refinery runs.
Differentials for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude were unchanged at $2.30 under November WTI.
Outright prices for Alaskan grade rose 25 cents from Friday to $22.55/22.85 a barrel, in line with heating oil-led gains in crude.
Line 63 diffs remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for November delivery.
Kern River, from California's San Joaquin Valley, rose with postings to 16.80/17.00 a barrel.
And prices for Long Beach-based Wilmington crude also tracked higher postings to $18.15/18.25 a barrel.
